sources.name: Xing Patel
sources.quote: I've been enjoying my retirement. The A's games have been exciting lately, and I was able to trade an extra ticket for a promise from someone to bring their kid next time. It's been nice to have more free time and be able to watch the games with my family.

sources.name: Marcus Osei
sources.quote: What's rattling me is seeing how many folks in Chinatown are struggling, and it's not just us. Downtown Oakland's got its own issues. If 13 people there are making headlines, that's 13 too many. We need to make sure our economic development plans are actually helping people on the ground, not just the ones with the loudest voices.

sources.name: Dillon Trevor
sources.quote: I've seen the neighborhood change a lot lately. Rents are going up, and it's getting harder to make ends meet. I'm not sure how much longer I can stay here, but I love the energy of Downtown. The A's games are always a highlight, and it's great to see fans gathering to talk about the game, even on rainy nights.

limits.rule: The Packet is what you know, not the fence around what you may write. The approved facts and the ledger are canon: never contradict them, and never import real-world Oakland (its people, businesses, landmarks, troubles). Everything else — the scene, the street, the weather in the room, unnamed people and what they say, new in-world places and businesses, what the city is talking about — is yours to invent; that colour is the job, and it never rewrites a canon fact. reviewProfile.purpose: Put the cycle's person events in the paper as news, one person at a time — a birth, a death, a hospital stay, a retirement, a promotion, a household set up or a place of one's own, a win or a loss on the book, what a turn of the city did to someone's day, and the smaller moments the record kept. approvedQuotes.text: I've been enjoying my retirement. The A's games have been exciting lately, and I was able to trade an extra ticket for a promise from someone to bring their kid next time. It's been nice to have more free time and be able to watch the games with my family.

What's rattling me is seeing how many folks in Chinatown are struggling, and it's not just us. Downtown Oakland's got its own issues. If 13 people there are making headlines, that's 13 too many. We need to make sure our economic development plans are actually helping people on the ground, not just the ones with the loudest voices.

I've seen the neighborhood change a lot lately. Rents are going up, and it's getting harder to make ends meet. I'm not sure how much longer I can stay here, but I love the energy of Downtown. The A's games are always a highlight, and it's great to see fans gathering to talk about the game, even on rainy nights.
